newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Abbey says not in talks with anyone.
newsitem.headline: Abbey says not in talks with anyone.

text.p: Abbey National Plc chairman Lord Tugendhat said on Friday that the British bank was not in discussions with National Westminster Plc or anybody else.
"We are not in discussions with them nor with anybody else for that matter," he told Reuters in an interview in Hong Kong.
"We had an approach (by NatWest) and we considered it, and we would consider any serious proposition," he said.
Tugendhat said Abbey National had no desire to be involved in investment banking or corporate relationships or with small or medium sized companies.
"The fact that we are not in certain activities which other banks are is as a result of a deliberate decision on our part," he said.

"What the speculation has shown -- which is interesting -- is that it has brought home to people the fact that Abbey National is a company with pretty much the same market capitalisation as NatWest and that our record by comparison with other banks in the U.K. is one that very few other people can match," Tugendhat said.
"We have a right to say that we are confident that we can continue to do it in the future," he added.

The Sunday Telegrah said on June 8 that Abbey National chief executive Peter Birch had previously spoken in favour of a merger with NatWest, but opposition was so intense the Abbey National board had unanimously rejected the proposal.
